guidance.heading: Financial Outlook
section: For the full year 2026, we are maintaining our top-line guidance. We continue to expect revenue to grow at a low- to mid-teens percentage on a year-over-year basis. We also continue to expect bookings to grow at a low-teens percentage on a year-over-year basis. Growth is anticipated to be driven by Base44’s continued strong growth trajectory through the remainder of the year.

For fourth quarter 2026, we expect revenue to grow at a low-double-digits percentage on a year-over-year basis and expect fourth quarter bookings growth to continue to lag revenue growth as a result of the more immediate impact of Partners softness on bookings.

For full year 2026, we now expect FCF margin excluding acquisition-related and restructuring costs to be approximately 16%, down from the high-teens previously anticipated, primarily due to accelerated sales and marketing investments in Base44. This outlook still assumes Base44 non-GAAP gross margin of approximately 60% in 2H with margin exiting the year above 60%. We expect further gross margin improvement to be reinvested into Base44 sales and marketing in the fourth quarter in order to position ourselves well to capture the continued elevated demand for Base44.

Our aggressive push into marketing is paying off - this is clearly reflected in Base44’s milestone ARR of nearly $250 million today. With the majority of Base44 subscriptions billed monthly and growth expected to ramp through the latter half of the year, we expect the strong ARR momentum this year to gradually translate into bookings and revenue dollars over the coming quarters.
In addition, we expect a working capital headwind in the fourth quarter of ~$10 million related to the prepayment of GPUs required to run our models for the next couple of years.

desk.headline: Revenue up 13% to $570.2m, slight beat; adjusted EPS $1.42 beat but down y/y; full-year FCF margin cut to ~16% as Base44 marketing grows

other.label: Base44 ARR
other.change: company figure, as of results date

results: Revenue rose 13% to $570.2m: Creative Subscriptions +14% to $406.7m and Business Solutions +10% to $163.5m; bookings grew a slower 11%.
Base44, the AI app builder, is near $250m of annual recurring revenue; its non-GAAP gross margin rose to 58% from near zero in Q1.
Selling and marketing costs jumped 41% to $193.2m as Wix spent heavily to win Base44 users, so non-GAAP operating margin fell to 12% from 18%.
GAAP net loss was $13.7m ($0.32 a share); adjusted EPS fell to $1.42 from $1.68 but was above the $1.35 estimate.
Partners revenue (agencies and resellers) grew 11% to $212.4m; co-founder Nir Zohar was named co-CEO alongside Avishai Abrahami.

guidance.summary: Wix kept its 2026 revenue (low- to mid-teens growth) and bookings (low-teens growth) targets, but cut its 2026 free cash flow margin target to about 16% from high-teens, mainly because of extra Base44 marketing. Q4 revenue is seen growing at a low-double-digit rate.

items.metric: FCF margin (excl. acquisition and restructuring costs)

points: The CEO called Base44 the company's "biggest bet" and said the heavy spending behind it is necessary.
The CFO said the first year-old Base44 user group renewed above expectations, and annual plans rose to over 20% of new sign-ups from about 5%.
Base44 gross margin is expected to exit 2026 above 60% and near the core business next year, helped by Wix's own in-house model cutting running costs.
Further margin gains in Q4 will be put back into Base44 marketing; a ~$10m Q4 cash outflow is expected for prepaid GPU capacity.
Bookings growth is expected to keep trailing revenue in Q4 because of weakness in the Partners business.
call.source: CEO and CFO comments in the results release; 24/7 Wall St. and Ynetnews, 10 Nov 2026 (no full call transcript found)

watch: Whether Base44 recurring revenue keeps turning into bookings and revenue as most plans are billed monthly.
Marketing spend and free cash flow margin in Q4 against the new ~16% target.
Partners softness and how the new co-CEO split works out.
